claim: A 2025 reanalysis of the Good Judgment Project found that adding extraneous variables substantially eliminated, reduced or even reversed the teaming and training effects on latent forecasting ability.
quote: substantially eliminated, reduced, and, in some cases, even reversed the effects
title: Rethinking the Role of Teams and Training in Geopolitical Forecasting: The Effect of Uncontrolled Method Variance on Statistical Conclusions
transfer: Do not treat human forecasting training (base rates, decomposition) as proven. Each agent step must pass our own equal-token test.

claim: The same reanalysis says latent traits tied to strategic responding can tell superforecasters from non-superforecasters, so the cause of their edge is hard to identify.
quote: latent traits associated with strategic responding can discriminate between superforecasters and non-superforecasters
title: Rethinking the Role of Teams and Training in Geopolitical Forecasting
transfer: Superforecaster habits may be partly tournament gaming. Prefer mechanisms that are scored against real outcomes in code.

claim: An LLM retrieval-and-ensemble forecasting system nears the crowd aggregate of competitive human forecasters and sometimes beats it.
quote: On average, the system nears the crowd aggregate of competitive forecasters, and in some settings surpasses it.
title: Approaching Human-Level Forecasting with Language Models
n: questions from forecasting platforms after model cutoffs
transfer: Pipeline of retrieve, reason, ensemble is a template for a forecast-type route. The earlier brief's Brier 0.240 figure was not on the abstract page and stays unverified.

claim: A crowd of twelve LLMs was not statistically different from 925 human forecasters on 31 binary questions, and showed an acquiescence bias toward yes.
quote: the LLM crowd outperforms a simple no-information benchmark and is not statistically different from the human crowd
title: Wisdom of the Silicon Crowd: LLM Ensemble Prediction Capabilities Rival Human Crowd Accuracy
transfer: Ensemble across different models, not samples of one model. Add a yes-bias correction on binary probability outputs.

claim: Showing GPT-4 and Claude 2 the human median improved accuracy 17 to 28 percent, but plain averaging of human and machine forecasts was more accurate.
quote: Both models' forecasting accuracy benefits from exposure to the median human prediction as information
title: Wisdom of the Silicon Crowd
transfer: Combine the agent's estimate with an external anchor by averaging in code rather than asking the model to revise toward it.

claim: On ForecastBench, expert forecasters outperform the top LLM (p < 0.001) in the original paper.
quote: expert forecasters outperform the top-performing LLM
authors: Karger, Bastani, Yueh-Han, Jacobs, Halawi, Zhang, Tetlock
title: ForecastBench: A Dynamic Benchmark of AI Forecasting Capabilities
transfer: Use as a contamination-free test bed for any forecast route. The abstract does not give the 0.017 Brier gap from the earlier brief; that comes from blog posts.

claim: AIA Forecaster reports parity with human superforecasters on ForecastBench but underperforms market consensus on a harder market benchmark; an ensemble with the market beats the market alone.
quote: an ensemble combining AIA Forecaster with market consensus outperforms consensus alone
title: AIA Forecaster: Technical Report
transfer: Treat an external market or crowd price as one input to average with, since the model adds information but does not replace it.

claim: Frontier LLM Brier scores ostensibly surpass the human crowd but still significantly underperform a group of expert forecasters.
quote: still significantly underperform a group of experts
title: Evaluating LLMs on Real-World Forecasting Against Expert Forecasters
transfer: Beating a casual crowd is a weak bar. Judge the agent against expert-level baselines.

claim: A 14B reasoning model trained with outcome-based RL on forecasting matched or surpassed o1 accuracy and greatly improved calibration.
quote: match or surpass the predictive accuracy of frontier models like o1
title: Outcome-based Reinforcement Learning to Predict the Future
transfer: Median of several sampled predictions at inference is a cheap step. Training is outside our one-model setup.

claim: Logical consistency checks across related questions (an arbitrage metric) correlate with LLM forecasters' later ground-truth Brier scores.
quote: our (instantaneous) consistency metrics correlate with LLM forecasters' ground truth Brier scores
authors: Paleka, Sudhir, Alvarez, Bhat, Shen, Wang, Tramer
title: Consistency Checks for Language Model Forecasters
transfer: New step: ask a question and its negation or a logical neighbour, check the probabilities obey the rules in code. Gives a confidence signal with no ground truth.

claim: A pastcasting benchmark (frozen web, resolved questions) gives results comparable to live internet forecasting and tracks capability progress over time.
quote: our pastcasting environment can produce results comparable to those based on forecasts using the internet on at-the-time unresolved questions
authors: Wildman, Bosse, Hnyk, Muhlbacher et al. (FutureSearch)
title: Bench to the Future: A Pastcasting Benchmark for Forecasting Agents
transfer: Lets us test forecast-route steps immediately on resolved questions with a fixed retrieval set.

claim: Asking RLHF models to verbalise confidence is typically better calibrated than their token probabilities, often cutting expected calibration error by about half.
quote: typically better-calibrated than the model's conditional probabilities
authors: Tian, Mitchell, Zhou, Sharma, Rafailov, Yao, Finn, Manning
title: Just Ask for Calibration
n: TriviaQA, SciQ, TruthfulQA; ChatGPT, GPT-4, Claude
transfer: If a stated number is needed, elicit it in words; still prefer agreement and checks as the main signal.

claim: LLMs are overconfident when stating confidence, calibration improves with scale, and no elicitation technique consistently wins; all struggle on professional-knowledge tasks.
quote: none of these techniques consistently outperform others
authors: Xiong, Hu, Lu, Li, Fu, He, Hooi
title: Can LLMs Express Their Uncertainty? An Empirical Evaluation of Confidence Elicitation in LLMs
transfer: Do not trust one prompt style for confidence. Calibrate per task class on our own logs.

claim: Consistency among multiple responses and better aggregation reduce overconfidence in verbalised confidence.
quote: human-inspired prompts, consistency among multiple responses, and better aggregation strategies
title: Can LLMs Express Their Uncertainty?
transfer: Support for using sample agreement as a confidence input, with the caveat that same-model samples are correlated.

claim: Large models are well calibrated on multiple choice and true/false in the right format, and P(True) self-evaluation shows encouraging calibration.
quote: larger models are well-calibrated on diverse multiple choice and true/false questions
title: Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
transfer: Cheap P(True) check on a proposed answer in multiple-choice format. P(IK) calibrates worse on new tasks, so avoid it as a gate.

claim: Semantic entropy, which groups sampled answers by meaning, predicts QA accuracy better than comparable baselines and needs no model changes.
quote: Our method is unsupervised, uses only a single model, and requires no modifications to off-the-shelf language models.
title: Semantic Uncertainty: Linguistic Invariances for Uncertainty Estimation in Natural Language Generation
transfer: Route step: cluster the probe attempts by meaning and use entropy as the escalate signal.

claim: Reasoning models were strictly better calibrated than non-reasoning counterparts in 33 of 36 settings, and calibration improved along the chain of thought.
quote: strictly better confidence calibration than their non-reasoning counterparts in 33 out of the 36 settings
title: Reasoning Models Better Express Their Confidence
transfer: Read confidence at the end of a long reasoning chain, not at the start. Slow-thinking behaviours (backtracking) matter.

claim: Removing slow-thinking behaviours from the chain of thought sharply reduces calibration, and non-reasoning models improve when prompted to think slowly with examples.
quote: removing slow thinking behaviors from the CoT leads to a significant drop in calibration
title: Reasoning Models Better Express Their Confidence
transfer: A slow-thinking prompt before the confidence statement is a testable step. Gate it, as forced doubt hurt us on single-answer tasks.

claim: Reasoning models are often overconfident (stated confidence above 85 percent even when wrong) and deeper reasoning can make it worse; introspection helped o3-Mini and R1 but made Claude 3.7 Sonnet worse.
quote: self-verbalized confidence estimates often greater than 85% particularly for incorrect responses
authors: Mei, Zhang, Yin, Lidard, Shorinwa, Majumdar
title: Reasoning about Uncertainty: Do Reasoning Models Know When They Don't Know?
transfer: Model-specific: test any introspection step on our own model. It conflicts with b-17, so do not assume either.

claim: Reasoning-trained models say I do not know much less often on factual tasks and report higher confidence with shorter reasoning, a possible reasoning tax.
quote: models tend to express higher confidence when providing shorter or less elaborate reasoning
title: Thinking Out Loud: Do Reasoning Models Know When They're Right?
transfer: Code-side floor and ceiling on confidence rather than trusting the model to abstain on factual questions.

claim: For LLM agents, step-level calibration does not imply trajectory-level calibration, step errors are coupled, own-response confidence does not consistently beat a simple baseline, and averaging hides late-stage overconfidence.
quote: averaging all trajectories together can hide overconfidence at later stages
authors: Lin, Lan, Guan, Jing, Fan, Gregg, Botterweck
title: Uncertainty Quantification for LLM Agents: A Taxonomy, an Evaluation Protocol, and an Empirical Study
transfer: Log confidence per step and score by step index. Do not average over a run. Earlier brief's arXiv id is confirmed real.

claim: The Satopaa-Pemantle-Ungar arXiv listing 1501.06943 was withdrawn as a mistaken separate submission; its model links optimal extremizing to forecasters' information overlap.
quote: varies as a function of the forecasters' information overlap
title: Combining Probability Forecasts and Understanding Probability Extremizing through Information Diversity
transfer: Extremize only when overlap is low. Same-model samples overlap heavily, so start the factor near 1 and tune on held-out. Cite 1406.2148, not the withdrawn id.
